paper_metadata.title: Novel Quantum Circuit Designs of Random Injection and Payoff Computation for Financial Risk Assessment

summary: The paper presents two Qiskit-based gate-model circuits for finance: an amplitude-estimation random-injection circuit evaluated with 8 parallel threads and 1,600 shots, and a 5-qubit payoff-computation circuit over prices 0–31 with strike price 24. Reported quantitative results include a 0.25 sign-change probability for random injection, a 9.26% average error for that histogram test, and payoff errors reduced from 3.912% to 0.0134% after calibration, with LM error reduced from 3.248% to 0.0079%.

experiments.description: Quantum amplitude estimation-based random injection circuit for financial risk assessment, implemented and evaluated in Qiskit with 8 parallel threads and 1600 measurement shots; compares random-injection behavior against deterministic grid sampling equivalence.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Amplitude Estimation (QAE) with random injection

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 8-thread parallel circuit; random variable r injected as a 2-bit discrete uniform variable over {0,1,2,3}; observation function g(x)=f(x) XOR (r==3)
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the expected value of a randomized payoff/risk function using QAE; E[g(x)] = 3/4 f(x) + 1/4 (f(x) XOR 1)

problem_instance.description: Financial risk assessment / random simulation toy example demonstrating random injection equivalence to exhaustive grid sampling

dataset_specification.description: Illustrative 8-thread and 2^66-thread scaling discussion; no real market dataset specified

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Histogram analysis and comparison to expected sign-change probability; average error reported over 1600 shots

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: None reported beyond defining the random variable and circuit structure
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Histogram/average error comparison against expected probability

speedup_claims.conditions: QAE-based estimation with random injection; paper claims convergence improves from O(m^-1/2) to O(m^-1)
speedup_claims.caveats: Claim is based on asymptotic analysis and equivalence to exhaustive grid sampling; no runtime benchmark or hardware speedup measurement is reported.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(m^-1) convergence claimed for QAE-based estimation
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(m^-1/2) for Monte Carlo sampling (as stated in paper discussion)

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No hardware benchmark or runtime comparison; only 8-thread toy circuit and 1600 shots in Qiskit
limiting_factors: Only a toy 8-thread example is shown
QAE advantage is asymptotic and not tied to a practical crossover size
Classical Monte Carlo baseline is discussed only theoretically

notes: Hardware is reported only as 'implemented on IBM Qiskit'; no specific backend/device is named, so hardware.type is left not_specified and provider set to IBM from framework context.

The paper does not explicitly state the total qubit count for the random-injection circuit; it discusses 8 threads and 2^66 scaling, but no exact register size is given for the implemented experiment.
Authors claim quadratic speedup via QAE and state convergence improves from O(m^-1/2) to O(m^-1), but provide no runtime benchmark or hardware advantage demonstration.

experiments.description: Quantum payoff computation circuit that filters prices at or above a strike threshold and computes weighted average payoff entirely within the quantum circuit; evaluated with 5-bit stock price encoding and 1600 Monte Carlo-style iterations for comparison.

algorithm.variant: Quantum payoff computation with mixed-signal switch / QAE-compatible averaging

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 5 qubits A~E encode stock prices 0..31; AB=11 acts as a digital control switch to route the LM qubit to PF when price >= 24
problem_formulation.objective_function: Compute payoff/weighted average only over prices meeting the strike threshold; PF = sum_i P[i+24]·(i·m+k) and LM = sum_i (P_i+P_i+8+P_i+16+P_i+24)·(i·m+k)
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Threshold filtering via mixed-signal switch; values below strike are ignored (PF=0)

problem_instance.description: Option-pricing / payoff computation toy instance with 5-bit stock prices and fixed strike price 24 (binary 11000)

dataset_specification.description: Prices 0..31; 16 of 32 prices have nonzero probability in the illustrated histogram

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: For alternative strike prices, inputs can be shifted by subtraction before circuit execution (e.g., strike 26 via subtracting 2 to map to strike 24)
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison of quantum circuit output against classical computation; error reported for original vs calibrated/Taylor-series formulations

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical comparison calculations; optional input shifting for alternative strike prices
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Weighted averaging and error comparison against classical baseline

speedup_claims.conditions: Paper claims the payoff circuit removes the need for classical pre-analysis and can execute payoff computation entirely within the quantum circuit
speedup_claims.caveats: No asymptotic speedup, oracle-query reduction, or wall-clock benchmark is reported for the payoff circuit.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 5-qubit circuit, 1600 iterations/shots, Qiskit implementation, classical comparison only
limiting_factors: No runtime or resource advantage over classical methods is reported
Problem size is tiny (5 qubits, 32 price states)
Classical preprocessing is still discussed for comparison and calibration
The paper reports accuracy improvements, not quantum advantage

notes: The paper explicitly states the circuit uses 5 bits (Price=ABCDE) to represent stock price variations, so num_qubits=5 is reported.
No specific backend/device, depth, gate counts, or noise model are given; Qiskit is the only implementation framework named.

The paper claims improved accuracy and elimination of classical preprocessing, but does not provide a formal asymptotic speedup analysis for this payoff circuit, so speedup_order is inferred as none_proven.
The paper claims the circuit can perform payoff computation entirely within the quantum circuit and reduce error from 3.912% to 0.0134%, but does not demonstrate practical quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Classical baseline comparison for the payoff-computation experiment: classical computation with input x=0.785+0.0157i, original quantum computation y=x=0.785+0.0157i, quantum computation with analog calibration y=0.785+0.01i, and Taylor-series-based computation using x=1/2+0.01i.
key_results: Classical baseline used as reference in Fig. 6
LM error: 3.248% reduced to 0.0079% after analog calibration
